title: Dataset Distillation Efficiently Encodes Low-Dimensional Representations from Gradient-Based Learning of Non-Linear Tasks
claim: Distilled data from one-step gradient methods recovers low-dimensional structure and beats random data, though it trails full-data training.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, log-scale y-axis, shaded confidence bands, shared legend
description: Two side-by-side line plots, each with MSE loss on a log-scale y-axis. The left plot has log_d N on the x-axis (1 to 5). The right plot has log_d J* on the x-axis (1 to 5). Six colored curves with translucent confidence bands are compared: Vanilla Training (blue), Teacher Training at t=2 (orange), Random I (green), One-Step GM (red), One-Step PM (purple) and Random II (brown). In the left plot, the distilled-data methods (red, purple, orange) fall steadily from about 10^0 to about 10^-1. The random baselines stay flat near 10^0. Vanilla training drops lowest, to about 10^-2. In the right plot, vanilla training is a flat line near 6x10^-3. The distilled curves decline from about 1 to 0.07, while the random baselines stay flat near 1. Wide red and blue shaded regions on the left side show high variance. A legend sits inside each plot.
caption: Reconstruction percentage when using $\mathcal D_2^S$ with different size ($1,10,50,100$) constructed following Lemma [ref] and its compact variant with respect to the MSE of teacher training $t=2$ (MSE loss) and the maximal attainable rank $L^\ast+1$ (Rank), for $r=3$ (left) and $r=10$ (right). d was set to $100$.
abstract: Dataset distillation, a training-aware data compression technique, has recently attracted increasing attention as an effective tool for mitigating costs of optimization and data storage. However, progress remains largely empirical. Mechanisms underlying the extraction of task-relevant information from the training process and the efficient encoding of such information into synthetic data points remain elusive. In this paper, we theoretically analyze practical algorithms of dataset distillation applied to the gradient-based training of two-layer neural networks with width $L$. By focusing on a non-linear task structure called multi-index model, we prove that the low-dimensional structure of the problem is efficiently encoded into the resulting distilled data. This dataset reproduces a model with high generalization ability for a required memory complexity of $\tildeÎ$$(r^2d+L)$, where $d$ and $r$ are the input and intrinsic dimensions of the task. To the best of our knowledge, this is one of the first theoretical works that include a specific task structure, leverage its intrinsic dimensionality to quantify the compression rate and study dataset distillation implemented solely via gradient-based algorithms.
